current.text: He is locked into the Pelicans starting lineup with Dejounte Murray and Zion Williamson.
Much of last season's usage came while Dejounte Murray, Herb Jones and others were out. Murray is expected to have the ball in his hands this season.
His usage and his minutes (about 36 per game last season) are expected to drop.
His fair auction price is in the mid 20s USD. 21 USD is good value, and he is sometimes overrated.
Experts disagree on his rank. One ranks him 22nd in 8-cat roto. Others call 9-cat rankings around 12th to 20th absurd and say his Yahoo rank near 35 is too high.
His ESPN rank of 45 and ESPN ADP of 77 are too low.
The Pelicans reportedly want about three first-round picks and a young player in a trade for him.
His trade value is at its peak because of his team-friendly contract.
The Pelicans lack shooting, and he is basically their only floor spacer.
New coach Jamahl Mosley brings a defense-first identity to a crowded rotation of about eight players who could start.
The Pelicans are projected to win about 34 games and miss the playoffs, near the bottom of the West.

durable.text: He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.
He has no weak category. His best categories are threes, FT% on good volume, points and steals.

note: He is a solid category player with no weak category, so he fits any build. He helps most in threes, FT% on good volume, points and steals. Experts price him in the mid 20s USD (Josh paid 21 USD). Yahoo values him at 29 USD, ESPN at 13 USD, and he cost 20 USD in our league last season, so a target of about 20 to 25 USD makes sense and anything near 30 USD is too much. Early in the season, check how his shots and minutes hold up with Dejounte Murray healthy under new coach Mosley, and watch for trade news.
